messages:
Alex W: quick q — opened a PR that updates the top-level CODEOWNERS to add a new glob for `infra/services/*` so platform-tools can auto-assign. wondering who is the canonical approver for that? PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/421 :thinking:

Sana P: if it's only adding a pattern that maps to an existing team, usually the team listed in the file owns it. but changing the top-level CODEOWNERS that affects many repos? ping @Jeremy K and @Maria L to confirm overlap with eng-platform rules.

Jeremy K: fyi, changes to the top-level CODEOWNERS that widen ownership need an eng-platform sign-off if they alter routing for infra services we operate. small tweak: if the entry references an external team (e.g., @security), get that team's ACK too.

Maria L: +1 to Jeremy. also: show the diff you planned. small example of risky change is adding `infra/*` which could shadow individual service owners. can you paste the snippet?

Alex W: pasted snippet in PR description but copying here:
```
# new entry in CODEOWNERS
infra/services/*  @platform-tools-team
```

Jeremy K: that exact glob will route a lot of existing repos to platform-tools — needs a rollout plan. options: (1) land with a canary list of repos, (2) add an explicit comment in CODEOWNERS explaining intent, (3) create a follow-up PR to add per-repo exceptions. you need an eng-platform + platform-tools approval.

Kevin T: if you add the platform-tools handle in the PR and tag @platform-tools-team in the description, one approver from that team + one from eng-platform should be fine. if this touches security-sensitive services, add @security as reviewer.

Alex W: noted. timeline: i'd like to merge before the infra day tomorrow morning so the auto-assigns work for a migration script. is that realistic?

Maria L: maybe — only if we do a canary and we have platform-tools approve today. i can give the eng-platform approval once the canary list is added and an exception plan exists.

Sana P: tagging on-call rotation: can we also add an owners file in the affected repos as a short-term opt-out? quick script can open PRs to add `OWNERS: platform-tools` or an exception comment.

deploy-bot: CI passed for PR #421 — all checks green (unit, lint, infra-integration). :white_check_mark:

Alex W: thanks. i added a canary list (infra/services/auth, infra/services/kv) and a short comment in CODEOWNERS explaining scope. added @platform-tools-team in reviewers.

Kevin T: i pulled the PR — looks good. i'll ping the platform-tools slack channel for a reviewer. pinged them: <https://redwood.slack.com/archives/CPLATFORM|#platform-tools> :rocket:

Maria L: saw the ping. if platform-tools approves in the next 2 hrs i can approve after a quick checkout. otherwise please don't merge until we confirm exceptions.

Sana P: i can do a fast follow PR to add per-repo OWNERS exceptions if we discover collisions.

Alex W: sweet — @platform-tools-team approved (one ack in PR). moving to eng-platform review. @Jeremy K can you give the final?

Jeremy K: reviewed locally, no surprises. approving now. land it and keep an eye on auto-assigns in the morning, revert plan prepared. :thumbsup:

Alex W: merging now. thanks everyone! :tada:

Kevin T: nice! will monitor the assigner logs.

Maria L: leaving a post-merge note in the weekly infra update about the change and the canary outcome.

Sana P: if anything odd pops up i'll open the exception PR.

Alex W: last message — merged and deploy job queued. thanks all.

deploy-bot: deploy job started for infra repo (deploy/infra 2026-03-17T09:12:00Z).
